{{Tooltip|L|Lost}} 63–65 vs. [[2024–25 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]] }} [[File:The Alamodome after Houston's win over Duke in the 2025 Final Four in San Antonio.jpg|alt=The Alamodome after Houston's win over Duke in the 2025 Final Four in San Antonio|thumb|254x254px|The [[Alamodome]] after Houston's 70–67 win over [[2024–25 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] in the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2025 Final Four]] in [[San Antonio]]]] {{2024–25 Big 12 men's basketball standings}} The '''2024–25 Houston Cougars men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Houston]] in the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Cougars were led by 11th-year head coach [[Kelvin Sampson]]. The team played their home games at the [[Fertitta Center]] as second-year members of the [[Big 12 Conference]]. With a win over [[2024–25 Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball team|Cincinnati]] on March 1, 2025, the Cougars clinched their second straight outright Big 12 regular season conference championship.{{Cite web |agency=Associated Press |date=2025-03-02 |title=No. 4 Houston clinches Big 12 regular-season title with 73-64 win over Cincinnati |url=https://www.lonestarlive.com/college/2025/03/no-4-houston-clinches-big-12-regular-season-title-with-73-64-win-over-cincinnati.html |access-date=2025-03-04 |website=lonestarlive |language=en}} As the No. 1 seed in the [[2025 Big 12 men's basketball tournament]], held at [[T-Mobile Center]] in [[Kansas City, Missouri]], Houston received a bye to the quarterfinals. There, they defeated [[2024–25 Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball team|Colorado]], 77–68, to advance to the semifinals, where they defeated [[2024–25 BYU Cougars men's basketball team|BYU]], 74–54, to advance to the championship game, where they secured a 72–64 victory over [[2024–25 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]] to claim their first tournament title. As the tournament champion, Houston received an automatic bid to the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2025 NCAA tournament]], also as the No. 1 seed. They were seeded in the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament#Midwest regional – Indianapolis, Indiana|Midwest region]]. There, they defeated [[2024–25 SIU Edwardsville Cougars men's basketball team|SIU Edwardsville]], 78–40, in the first round, [[2024–25 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team|Gonzaga]], 81–76, in the second round, [[2024–25 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]], 62–60, in the Sweet Sixteen, and [[2024–25 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]], 69–50, in the Elite Eight to advance to their first Final Four since 2021. In the Final Four, they overcame a 14-point deficit to defeat [[2024–25 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]], 70–67, to advance to their first [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|national championship]] since [[1984 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|1984]]. In the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|championship game]], despite leading for nearly the entire game – the same thing Duke did to them in the Final Four – Houston ultimately lost to [[2024–25 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]], 65–63, denying them their first national title.{{Cite web |last=FOX 26 Digital |first= |date=2025-04-07 |title=Houston Cougars lose national title, fall to Florida |url=https://www.fox26houston.com/sports/houston-cougars-lose-national-title-fall-florida-draft |access-date=2025-07-22 |website=[[KRIV (TV)|FOX 26 Houston]] |language=en-US}} ==Previous season== The [[2023–24 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|Cougars]] finished the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2023–24 season]] 28–3, 15–3 in [[2023–24 Big 12 Conference men's basketball season|Big 12 play]] to win the regular season championship in their first year in the conference. They defeated [[2023–24 TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball team|TCU]] and [[2023–24 Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball team|Texas Tech]] to advance to the [[2024 Big 12 men's basketball tournament|Big 12 tournament]] championship game, where they lost to [[2023–24 Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball team|Iowa State]].{{Cite web |date=2024-03-16 |title=#1/1 Men's Hoops Falls to #7/8 Iowa State in Big 12 Title Game |url=https://uhcougars.com/news/2024/3/16/-1-1-men |access-date=2024-06-16 |website=uhcougars.com |language=en}} They received an at-large bid to the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 1 seed in the South Regional. They defeated [[2023–24 Longwood Lancers men's basketball team|Longwood]] in the First Round and [[2023–24 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Texas A&M]] in overtime in the Second Round to advance to their fifth consecutive Sweet Sixteen. There, they were defeated by [[2023–24 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] after losing starting point guard, [[Jamal Shead]], to an ankle sprain during the game.{{Cite web |date=2024-03-29 |title=#2/2 (1) Men's Hoops Falls to Duke in Sweet 16 |url=https://uhcougars.com/news/2024/3/29/mens-basketball-2-2-1-mens-hoops-falls-to-duke-in-sweet-16 |access-date=2024-06-16 |website=uhcougars.com |language=en}} ==Offseason== ===Departing players=== {| class="wikitable sortable" style="text-align: center" |+ style="{{NCAA color cell|Houston Cougars}}" | Houston departures |- align=center {{CollegeSecondaryHeader|team=Houston Cougars|Name|Number|Pos.|Height|Weight|Year|Hometown|Reason for departure}} |- | [[Jamal Shead]] || 1 || G || 6'1" || 200 || Senior || [[Manor, Texas|Manor, TX]] || Graduated/declared for the [[2024 NBA draft]];
